```{r setup, include=FALSE}
run <- requireNamespace("duckdb", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("dplyr", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("dbplyr", quietly = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = run)
```

## Overview

The ICIJ Offshore Leaks database holds records from the Panama Papers,
Pandora Papers and other leaks. `live_icij()` loads the ICIJ CSV files into
an in-memory DuckDB database and exposes four object types: `Entity`,
`Officer`, `Intermediary` and `Address`. A 20-row sample ships with the
package, so this vignette runs without a download.

## Loading the connection

```{r conn}
library(ontologyConnectR)
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)

# Uses the bundled sample
icij_con <- live_icij()

# Or point at the full ICIJ CSV download:
# icij_con <- live_icij(csv_dir = "~/data/icij")
```

## Describing the object types

Object types are defined with ontologySpecR. Property ids match the column
names `live_icij()` exposes (for example `entity_id` for the ICIJ `node_id`).

```{r bundle}
library(ontologySpecR)

entity <- object_type(
  "Entity",
  properties = list(
    property_def("entity_id", "integer"),
    property_def("name", "string"),
    property_def("jurisdiction", "string"),
    property_def("status", "string"),
    property_def("source_id", "string")
  ),
  primary_key = "entity_id"
)
officer <- object_type(
  "Officer",
  properties = list(
    property_def("officer_id", "integer"),
    property_def("name", "string"),
    property_def("countries", "string")
  ),
  primary_key = "officer_id"
)

icij_bundle <- bundle("icij", "1.0.0", objects = list(entity, officer))
```

## Building the context

```{r context}
ctx <- connect_context(
  icij_bundle,
  live_connections = list(Entity = icij_con, Officer = icij_con),
  strict = TRUE
)
ctx
```

## Querying entities

`dplyr` verbs are translated to SQL and pushed down to DuckDB when you call
`collect()`.

```{r query-entities}
bvi_panama <- connect_object_set(ctx, "Entity") |>
  filter(source_id == "Panama Papers", jurisdiction == "BVI") |>
  collect()

bvi_panama[, c("entity_id", "name", "status")]
```

```{r show-query}
connect_object_set(ctx, "Entity") |>
  filter(jurisdiction == "PAN") |>
  show_query()
```

## Officers of an entity

The `edges` file records relationships between nodes. Join it to officers to
find the people behind each entity:

```{r edges}
edges_path <- system.file("fixtures", "icij_sample", "edges.csv",
                          package = "ontologyConnectR")
edges <- utils::read.csv(edges_path)
officer_of <- edges[edges$rel_type == "officer_of", ]

officers <- collect(connect_object_set(ctx, "Officer"))
linked <- merge(officer_of, officers,
                by.x = "node_id_start", by.y = "officer_id")
head(linked[, c("name", "node_id_end", "rel_type")])
```

## Using objectSetsR instead

A `LiveConnection` is a DBI connection, so it also works with objectSetsR.
Call objectSetsR's functions fully qualified, so it is clear which
package's context you are using:

```{r objectsetsr, eval = FALSE}
os_ctx <- objectSetsR::ontology_context(icij_bundle, icij_con)
objectSetsR::object_set(os_ctx, "Entity")
```

objectSetsR reads the table name from `ontologySpecR::object_table()`, and
the live connection looks it up in its schema map, so leave `source_table`
unset (or set it to the object type id) for live-backed types.
